utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'San Dimas' by name among the cities in its service area.

value.name: Southern California Edison (SCE)
value.notes: Clean Power Alliance's own homepage states it serves '38 communities across Los Angeles and Ventura counties' and names each one individually via its site's community directory; San Dimas is not among the named communities. No other Los Angeles/Ventura County CCA serving San Dimas was found, so Southern California Edison (SCE) is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

county.notes: San Dimas is a well-documented Los Angeles County city; also listed under Los Angeles County in SCE's own service-area fact sheet.

permit_authority.value: City of San Dimas Building and Safety Division

permit_url.notes: Directly re-verified this session: the Building & Safety index page links a dedicated 'Solar Permit Center' page (S7), which fully describes the SolarAPP+ eligibility, application steps, and Planning Division site requirements. The main sandimasca.gov domain (as opposed to the files. subdomain used here) still returns HTTP 403.

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other SCE-territory records this session.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes San Dimas/Los Angeles County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: Approved SolarAPP+ documents and SolarAPP+ Approval number

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own 'Solar Permit Center' page, Step 4 of the online permit application: 'upload the approved SolarAPP+ documents, and any additional information relevant to your project such as structural calculations, spec sheets, etc.'

value: Schedule inspections through the City's online portal (Schedule Inspection tool)
The permit remains valid only if progress is verified by a passed inspection at least every six months
inspection_steps.notes: This is the City's general Building Division inspection process (the same page covers all building permit types, including solar); the City does not publish a separate, solar-specific inspection sequence. The page describes full-construction inspection stages (foundation, framing, etc.) in more detail than would apply to a typical rooftop PV installation, so only the generally-applicable scheduling/validity facts are recorded here.

timeline_days.notes: The City's own 'Solar Permit Center' page describes the SolarAPP+ and online-permit-center application steps in detail but does not state an explicit day count or 'instant'/'instantaneous' issuance language, so no timeline figure is recorded per the mission's strict explicit-evidence bar.

value.program_or_pathway: SolarAPP+ (roof-mounted residential PV, R3 occupancies only)
other_conditions: Ground-mounted PV (residential or commercial) and PV on commercial buildings cannot use SolarAPP+ or the City's online permitting center; call the Building Division for submittal requirements
Conduit must be painted to match the adjacent surface
Modules must maintain a minimum 12-inch distance from roof edges and ridges
The City prefers flush-mounted modules with no more than 6 inches between the finished roof and the bottom of the module
